title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover hysteresis
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring regional thrashing and cascade failovers during a high-rate traffic spike in production. Root cause analysis pointed to the SLO enforcer backoff logic: aggressive immediate backoff combined with insufficient hysteresis/quorum checks caused simultaneous load-shedding across regions and a feedback loop that made recovery slow. This PR introduces a conservative smoothing/hysteresis layer, a quorum-based region-unlock check, and tighter circuit-breaker state transitions to prevent simultaneous global shedding. Changes include: - implement exponential smoothing on short-term error-rate and latency signals to avoid reacting to single-step spikes - add region-level quorum check (min healthy nodes + recent-success threshold) before flipping from shed -> normal - separate short-term and long-term counters used by the enforcer (fast_fail_count vs sustained_fail_count) - require graceful ramp-down path: allow a percentage of requests through during backoff to probe recovery - avoid double-shed: if a global fallback has already been triggered, region enforcers no-op to prevent cascading - add feature-flag (runtime) to roll back quickly and A/B test heuristics - extensive unit + integration tests and a canary job in perf-canary for 48h. Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for smoothing and counters
- [x] Integration tests for quorum unlock logic
- [x] Perf canary job + dashboard links added
- [x] Add observability metrics for hysteresis windows and decision rationale
- [x] Feature flag gated changes for quick rollback

Backwards compatibility: runtime defaults preserve current behavior until feature-flag is enabled for canary customers. Rollout plan: enable on a single control-plane region, observe for 24h, then stagger to additional regions if stable. See linked Linear tickets for investigation notes and rollback plan.
